questions.stem: After Gram staining, an organism appears pink. Which cell-wall feature explains this?

options.B: Waxy wall rich in mycolic acid
options.C: No cell wall, with sterols in the membrane
options.D: Thin peptidoglycan with an outer membrane

questions.explanation: Gram-negative walls are decolorized by alcohol and take up safranin (pink). A: Gram-positive walls retain the violet. B: Mycolic acid walls (M. tuberculosis) are not Gram-stained; Ziehl-Neelsen is used. C: Wall-less Mycoplasma stain poorly. E: Capsules appear as an unstained halo.

questions.stem: Which component is responsible for fever and shock in Gram-negative sepsis?
questions.explanation: Lipid A is endotoxin, released on lysis. A: Teichoic acid is Gram-positive (adhesion). B: Peptidoglycan isn't the endotoxin. D: The O polysaccharide is the antigenic part. E: Porins are channels.

questions.stem: Surgical instruments are contaminated with Clostridium spores. Which method reliably destroys the spores?

options.B: Autoclaving with steam at 121 °C for 20 minutes

questions.explanation: Spores (dehydrated, calcium dipicolinate, metabolically inert, many layers) resist boiling and chemicals but are killed by autoclaving. A: Spores resist boiling. C: Spores resist chemical sterilization. D: UV kills vegetative bacteria, not reliably spores. E: Lysozyme damages vegetative cell walls (forms L-forms), not spores.

questions.stem: A UTI fails to respond to antibiotics because resistance genes spread from one E. coli strain to another. Which element most likely transferred them?
questions.explanation: Conjugative plasmids (large, F factor/tra gene, common in Gram-negative bacilli) form sex pili and transfer R genes between cells. A: Non-conjugative plasmids cannot transfer under normal conditions. B: Transposons move genes within a cell. C: Ordinary pili mediate adherence; sex pili mediate conjugation. D: Flagella give motility.

questions.stem: Which property distinguishes exotoxins from endotoxins?

options.B: Exotoxins can be converted into toxoids for vaccination
options.D: Exotoxins are released only on cell lysis

questions.explanation: Formalin-treated exotoxins become antigenic, non-toxic toxoids (tetanus, diphtheria). A: Lipid A is endotoxin. C: Exotoxins are heat-labile. D: Exotoxins are secreted by living cells. E: They are strongly immunogenic.

questions.stem: Penicillin-treated Gram-negative bacteria lose their walls but regrow them when the drug is removed. These forms are:
questions.explanation: Wall-deficient L-forms from Gram-negatives are spheroplasts and can revert. A: Mycoplasma genetically lacks a wall and doesn't revert. B: Protoplasts come from Gram-positives. D: Spores are resting forms. E: Acid-fast bacilli have waxy walls.

questions.stem: A 30-year-old man has fever, cough, and diarrhea after a hotel stay; the organism grows inside alveolar macrophages by blocking phagosome–lysosome fusion. Which organism shares this survival mechanism?
questions.explanation: Legionella and mycobacteria inhibit phagolysosome fusion. B: Listeria escapes the phagosome into the cytoplasm. C: S. aureus uses protein A and coagulase. D: S. pyogenes uses M protein. E: Neisseria uses pili and IgA protease.

questions.stem: A 2-year-old has repeated pneumococcal infections. Serotype-specific capsule swelling is seen when the isolate is mixed with antiserum. Which property makes the capsule a key virulence factor?

options.B: It degrades secretory IgA at mucosa

questions.explanation: Capsules are antiphagocytic; serotype-specific swelling (Quellung) is the basis of serotyping and vaccines. A: Lipid A is in the Gram-negative outer membrane. B: IgA protease is a Neisseria enzyme. C: Coagulase is a S. aureus enzyme. E: Pili are made of pilin, not capsule.

questions.stem: Staphylococci colonize an IV catheter within a loosely bound polysaccharide layer that protects them from antibiotics and immune cells. This layer is the:
questions.explanation: Slime (glycocalyx) is loosely attached and secreted, binding bacteria to each other and to catheters or valves as a biofilm. B: A capsule is firmly attached and well-defined. C: Staphylococci are Gram-positive with no outer membrane. D: A peptidoglycan cortex is part of a spore. E: Teichoic acid aids adhesion but is part of the cell wall.

questions.stem: A man with a crush injury develops rapidly spreading gas gangrene from Clostridium perfringens. Which enzyme degrades a fatty component of human tissue cell membranes?
questions.explanation: C. perfringens lecithinase degrades lecithin, a fatty component of human tissues. A: Collagenase (also C. perfringens) degrades collagen. B: Hyaluronidase degrades hyaluronic acid. C: Coagulase (S. aureus) converts fibrinogen to fibrin. D: Streptokinase (S. pyogenes) lyses fibrin clots.
